source.title: Understanding sparse autoencoder scaling in the presence of feature manifolds
source.authors: Eric J. Michaud; Liv Gorton; Tom McGrath

page_placements.theme: Manifold tiling: continuous features split across many localized latents or blocks

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates SAE scaling and manifold tiling using a capacity-allocation model and synthetic-manifold experiments, rather than measuring coarse-to-fine feature matches across dictionary sizes.
record.gate_note: The paper does not track a coarse latent in a smaller SAE to corresponding latents in a larger SAE or measure whether their firing sets partition the coarse latent's inputs. It does report toy-manifold tiling as SAE width increases, and tests how synthetic manifold geometry affects SAE loss scaling. Its real-model nearest-neighbor cosine measurements do not identify split families or concept hierarchies.
record.test_reason: The study measures SAE latents tiling continuous feature manifolds (circle, hyperspheres, shells) as width grows, plus nearest-neighbour decoder cosines in real SAEs. This is related to splitting but is a different construct. No coarse latent is matched to finer latents across widths, and no coverage of a parent's inputs, direction proximity, hierarchy, absorption or canonical-unit decomposition is measured. It therefore tests no version; its findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors adapt Brill's capacity-allocation model: when β<α, latents accumulate on common manifolds and feature discovery D(N)/N goes to 0. They cannot say whether real SAEs are in this regime because α and β are unknown. Their strongest counter-argument is that radial variation makes SAEs learn a ~2d basis rather than tile; they frame the work as posing the problem.
record.recipe_differences: The study models latent allocation and trains SAEs on synthetic manifolds, then measures decoder geometry on existing LLM and vision SAEs; it does not perform cross-width parent-child feature matching.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss-versus-width behavior depends on manifold geometry: hollow hyperspheres can show gradual scaling, while manifolds with radial variation plateau quickly. ReLU L1 and JumpReLU are both used for synthetic experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On a circle and on hollow hyperspheres, L1/JumpReLU SAEs keep lowering loss by tiling the manifold with more, sparser latents (β≈0.05 for dims 6–8). With radial variation, loss plateaus at ~2d_i latents (a basis solution).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether SAEs over-tile a continuous feature manifold as width grows depends on manifold geometry; radial intensity variation prevents tiling.

fits_no_version.finding: Real SAE decoder nearest-neighbour cosines are skewed above random. Gemma Scope shows few extreme (>0.97) pairs, and those have dead neighbours; Inception-v1 shows a meaningful high-similarity fraction, possibly duplicates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Real SAEs show limited evidence of dense manifold tiling by decoder-direction similarity.

record.problems: The authors explicitly say they do not know the true feature-frequency distribution or real-world feature-manifold geometry, so they cannot determine whether real SAEs scale pathologically. The main tiling and loss-scaling experiments use synthetic manifolds. Real-model geometry is measured with nearest-neighbor cosine similarity, which does not identify split families.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were added for individual dimensions in Figures 3 and 6 or individual Gemma Scope widths and sparsity settings: the text summarizes these results in aggregate, and the plots do not provide textual outcomes for each curve. Figure 4's latent firing-frequency slopes are discussed as speculative estimates of α, not as measurements of feature splitting or manifold tiling.

untested.parts: No matching of smaller-SAE latents to larger-SAE latents, no coverage measure, no direction proximity; only qualitative manifold tiling.
Gemma Scope widths are examined only for nearest-neighbour cosine, not splitting.
Absorption is only mentioned as violating the model's assumptions.
No decomposition of large-SAE latents into small-SAE latents.
No correlated or hierarchical inputs, and no Matryoshka or alternative-objective comparison of splitting.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked toy tiling rows to V1/V6 and gave labels. Tiling a continuous manifold resembles splitting but is not the claim's coarse-to-fine latent replacement. Nor is it splitting caused by correlated or hierarchical inputs, so all rows are relinked to none and no verdicts are given. The Figure 4 firing-frequency slopes (-0.74, -0.57) are α estimates, rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The study shows SAE latents tiling a toy manifold as width increases, but does not match parent and child latents across widths, establish that the larger latents collectively cover a smaller latent's inputs, or quantify their directional proximity.

The paper notes that absorption violates its modeling assumptions but does not measure whether parent latents fail to fire where child latents take over, or test changing size or sparsity as a remedy.
The study tests SAE tiling on synthetic manifolds, but not whether observed feature splitting says little about a model's own units, and does not test Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: ReLU SAE on S^1
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAEs of increasing width to reconstruct points on a circle with an L1 sparsity penalty.
rows.measure: Manifold tiling by latent firing regions; total SAE loss
rows.value: The 4-latent SAE is shown with latents firing on arcs of the circle; the text says SAEs can slightly reduce total loss by tiling the manifold with more sparsely activating latents.
rows.note: This is a toy-manifold tiling result, not a matched parent-to-children feature-splitting measurement.
rows.check: Qualitative Figure 1 of circle tiling at 4 latents. No cross-width matching of a coarse latent to finer latents, so it cannot show V1. It is not a correlated or hierarchical-input test of V6.

rows.subject: ReLU L1 SAE
rows.size_stated: not stated; curves shown over 1 to 10^4 latents
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAEs to reconstruct individual unit hyperspheres and measured loss as latent count increased.
rows.measure: Total SAE loss versus number of latents
rows.value: Figure-only curves; the text says some manifolds accommodate many thousands of latents without loss plateauing, and reports β roughly 0.05 for hyperspheres with dimension 6–8 over the measured range.
rows.note: This supports gradual loss reduction through allocating latents to some synthetic manifolds, not a measured parent-child split.
rows.check: Loss-vs-width on hollow hyperspheres (β≈0.05 for dims 6–8). This measures per-manifold loss scaling, not splitting of features or its relation to model units.

rows.subject: ReLU L1 SAE

rows.subject: Gemma Scope SAEs on gemma-2-2b layer 12 residual stream
rows.operation_detail: Measured the distribution of decoder-vector cosine similarities to each vector's nearest neighbor.
rows.baseline: Random decoder vectors are described as approximately orthogonal; no numeric reference value stated.
rows.value: The distribution is substantially skewed higher than the random-vector expectation, but the text says there is not overall a very large fraction of latents with extremely high nearest-neighbor cosine similarity.
rows.note: The measurement does not identify latents as members of a split family or test hierarchy.
rows.check: Nearest-neighbour cosine distribution in Gemma Scope does not identify split families; the link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Gemma Scope SAE, width 262k
rows.operation_detail: Investigated latents with very high nearest-neighbor decoder cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Count and status of latents with nearest-neighbor cosine similarity above 0.97
rows.value: For some SAEs, 10–100 latents have cosine similarity > 0.97 with their nearest neighbor; in the examined SAE, each investigated latent's nearest neighbor was dead across the dataset.
rows.note: The paper says these highly similar latents are not being used to sparsely reconstruct manifold points; it suggests they may be a training artifact.
rows.check: High-similarity latents have dead neighbours, which the authors read as a training artifact. This is not splitting.

rows.subject: ReLU L1 SAE on Inception-v1
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise cosine similarities between latent decoder directions.
rows.value: A meaningful fraction of latents have very high cosine similarity with their nearest neighbor; the paper notes this could be due to duplicated latents.
rows.note: No matched-width split families or hierarchy are measured.
rows.check: Inception-v1 high-similarity neighbours may be duplicates. This is not splitting.

relation.reason: Latent tiling of manifolds as width grows is related to splitting but is a different construct, and the paper does not test the claim.

tranche.reason: Studies SAE scaling on toy feature manifolds (tiling) and nearest-neighbour decoder cosines. It never matches coarse latents to finer latents across widths and never names feature splitting, so it measures a related but different construct. T6 fits; the reader's T2 guess is not supported.

source_check.notes: All rows are qualitative or figure-only (Figures 1, 3 and 6), and no per-width loss numbers are stated. Figure 1 says tiling lowers loss only 'slightly'. Hypersphere legends read S^1-S^8, so the rows' 'dimensions 2 through 9' is the ambient dimension. The paper does not resolve whether real SAEs are in the pathological regime.

statements.correction: Circle (Figure 1, ReLU L1): loss falls slightly or gradually by tiling, then plateaus after dozens of latents. Hollow hyperspheres: gradual L(n) scaling (A.1, Figures 3 and 6). Higher-dimensional spheres take at least 10^4 latents without a plateau (ReLU). Beta about 0.05 for dims 6-8 is measured on ReLU L1 SAEs (Figure 5). Radial variation (0.5<|x|<2): ReLU and JumpReLU plateau at n_i about 2d_i (basis solution). Gemma Scope gemma-2-2b layer 12: no very large fraction of extreme nearest-neighbour cosines. Some SAEs have 10-100 latents above 0.97. In one SAE (262k, L0 121), their neighbours were dead.
statements.problem: Overstates the circle result: Figure 1 says loss falls only 'slightly', and Sec 2.4 says the circle plateaus after dozens of latents. It also pins beta about 0.05 on 'L1/JumpReLU', but Figure 5 measures it only for ReLU L1. A.1 attributes gradual hypersphere scaling to Figures 3 and 6 together. The 10^4-latent figure is ReLU only. The radial-variation and Gemma Scope parts are right.
